raw.cause: logger's channel is created with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY (event -20327001, flags 0x4b), so when nav (priority 30, running at display's inherited priority inside nav_handle) does MsgSend to logger, logger's receiving thread stays at priority 10 instead of inheriting 30. media at priority 20 keeps both CPUs busy, preempts logger mid-request (109875 READY at 10, 109886/110750 media RUNNING at 20), and nav stays REPLY-blocked: e.g. 5432.8 to 5482.1 ms (109849 to 110899), and 5594.0 to 5644.0 ms (111883 to 112568), versus the normal ~2 ms.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (run_logger), served to nav's MsgSend
raw.fix_summary: Drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so logger inherits the priority of the waiting client (what COCKPIT_FIXED=1 already does), or simply use name_attach() like the other servers. If logging must really never compete with real work, change the contract instead: make log_line asynchronous (MsgSendPulse or a local queue drained by a low-priority thread) so nav never REPLY-blocks on a fixed-low-priority server.

finding: nav waits on logger behind lower priority work
